findings.title: TypeError crash when destinationCalendar is empty and location is Google Meet
findings.body: After the destinationCalendar is converted to an array, this fallback uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without an optional chain. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]` (which is a common case handled by every caller of this function, e.g. when the user selected Google Meet as the location but has no Google Calendar configured on Cal, which previously was a soft "fallback to Cal Video" path), `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = ... ?? []` yields `undefined`, and the next expression `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')`. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"` and would safely fall back to Cal Video; the new code crashes before the fallback can occur. This regression breaks the entire Meet-location code path for any booking without a Google destination calendar.

findings.title: Team destination calendars not added when no event-type or organizer calendar exists
findings.body: The event's `destinationCalendar` is set by the chain to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` is set. The subsequent line `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` uses optional chaining and silently no-ops on `null`. As a result, in the very scenario the PR is meant to fix — a COLLECTIVE event where the event-type has no destination calendar and the organizer (first host) has no destination calendar but other team members do — the team members' `destinationCalendar` values are never attached to `evt.destinationCalendar`, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` falls back to "the first connected calendar" instead of creating the event in each host's calendar. The push should be a normal assignment that initialises the array if needed, e.g. `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`. Also note that if `eventType.destinationCalendar` is set, pushing team members onto the same array may create duplicate references for the same DestinationCalendar record.

findings.title: Broken fallback for updateEvent when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: In `updateEvent`, the fallback for when `externalCalendarId` is not provided is now `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is `null`/undefined (which happens for legacy bookings stored before this PR that do not have `BookingReference.externalCalendarId` populated), the predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined` and never matches, so the result is `undefined`. The previous code `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` correctly fell back to the first destination calendar's externalId. With this change, update calls that previously succeeded now hit Google with `calendarId: undefined` and fail. The intent appears to be "pick the destination calendar for this credential", so the find should compare against `credentialId` (or the caller should pass it through), not against the already-undefined `externalCalendarId`. The same broken pattern is present in `deleteEvent` (see next finding).

findings.title: Broken fallback for deleteEvent when externalCalendarId is missing
findings.body: The deleteEvent fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` exhibits the same bug as updateEvent: when `externalCalendarId` is undefined/null, the predicate cannot match, so `calendarId` ends up `undefined` and Google receives a delete call without a `calendarId` (only the `defaultCalendarId = "primary"` ternary saves it when `calendarId` is falsy). For legacy bookings that don't store an externalCalendarId on the reference, this silently routes deletions to "primary" instead of the correct destination calendar. The fallback was `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` before this PR, and the rewrite removes that legitimate fallback without providing a working one.

findings.title: Team members may be excluded when first user in array is not the organizer
findings.body: The new `teamDestinationCalendars` is built from `users.slice(1)`, i.e. it always excludes whichever user happens to be at index 0 in the `users` array. For dynamic events `users` is populated from `prisma.user.findMany({ where: { username: { in: dynamicUserList } } })` with no `orderBy`, so the index-0 user may not be the organizer. If the actual organizer happens to be at index 0 they are correctly excluded (their calendar is taken from `organizerUser.destinationCalendar`), but if they are not, their `destinationCalendar` is lost from `teamDestinationCalendars` because `.slice(1)` indiscriminately cuts the first element. The exclusion should be keyed on whether the user is the organizer (e.g. by id/username), not on array index.
